formalObservation.Composition:
The composition consists primarily of two large figure-like structures positioned side-by-side.

- larger figure on the left
- smaller vertically oriented figure on the right
- both contained within strong geometric and curvilinear structural boundaries
formalObservation.Primary Forms:
- Large left figure
- Smaller right figure
- Upper horizontal structure
- Central vertical structural element
- Lower rounded forms
formalObservation.Left Figure — Visible Features:
- one prominent eye-like form
- large curved facial structure
- projecting central form
- mouth containing repeated triangular marks
- large rounded lower body
- small cluster of circular forms near lower portion
- several short lower projections
- strong outer contour
formalObservation.Right Figure — Visible Features:
- two circular/oval eye-like forms
- broad horizontal wavy mouth-like form
- rounded lower body
- long dark vertical/curved appendage along left side
- pair of lower projections
formalObservation.Structural Forms:
- large rectangular upper structure
- horizontal bar-like forms
- vertical supports
- large enclosing contour
- lower rounded/oval elements
formalObservation.Repeated Forms:
- Circular forms
- Oval forms
- Eye-like units
- Horizontal bands
- Parallel hatching
- Rounded lower structures
formalObservation.Mark-Making:
- heavy parallel hatching
- broad outer contours
- dense charcoal filling
- repeated horizontal strokes
- vertical directional marks
- lighter internal marks
formalObservation.Spatial Strategy:
Paired / Enclosed

The two major figures establish a left-right relationship within a shared structural field.
formalObservation.Formal Language:
- Large figure contrasted with smaller adjacent figure.
- Rectilinear structures frame organic forms.
- Circular units recur within anatomy-like structures.
- Heavy hatching establishes surrounding architectural field.
- Repetition occurs through eyes, rounded forms and horizontal bands.
- Composition depends more on adjacency and structural framing than overlap.
